note: These are Jev's judgments, not measurements: for each candidate, Jev (TypeSafe System One) chose the industry of the US economy that earned most of its revenue (`industry`: the choice, its confidence and the three likeliest with their probabilities) and placed how major a player it was in that industry in the United States at its peak on the five levels below (`major`: the probability-weighted level 0-4, its confidence, and `p`, the probability of each level), reading the opening of the company's English Wikipedia article. The roster (Tools/companies/build.py) is the companies scoring 2.0 or more plus the 75 curated ones, each in Jev's industry at confidence 0.6 or more and otherwise in the authored one.
state: `company`: name, ticker, years (authored in Tools/companies/candidates.json or company-lives.json) and description (the opening of its English Wikipedia article, the Wikimedia REST API's page summary, fetched by Tools/companies/fetch.py); `industries`: the 23 market industries of industries.json by id, name and NAICS coverage. Nothing else.

industry.instructions: `company` is a US company: its name, ticker, the years it existed and the opening of its English Wikipedia article (`company.description`). Which of these industries of the US economy earned most of `company.name`'s revenue, judging by its main business over its history and weighing most the years when it was largest? Pick the industry of what it sells, as the US national accounts class a business by its main activity, not the industry of its suppliers or of its customers.

major.instructions: `company` is a US company: its name, ticker, the years it existed and the opening of its English Wikipedia article (`company.description`). Its industry is the one of the 23 broad industries of the US economy listed in `industries` that earned most of its revenue. At its peak, at any time from 1947 to 2025, how large a player was `company.name` in that whole industry in the United States, beside all of the industry's US businesses, listed or privately held (not nonprofits or government bodies), and not only those of its own niche, by revenue, assets or market value?
criteria: A minor company of its industry: even at its peak it was small beside the industry's leading US companies, far below the largest dozen.
A mid-sized company of its industry: well known, but even at its peak it stayed below the twelve or so largest US companies of its industry.
At its peak, one of the larger dozen US companies of its industry, though not one of the five largest.
At its peak, one of the five largest US companies of its industry, though not its leader.
At its peak, the leader or co-leader of its industry in the United States: the industry's largest company, or one of its two largest.
